llm.summary: The skill's code, instructions, and requirements are consistent with its stated purpose (deregistering Consul services via the HTTP API); it requests no extra credentials or unusual installs and appears to do only the expected network calls to user-supplied Consul agents.

dimensions.detail: Name/description, SKILL.md examples, and the included Python script all implement the same functionality: sending Consul /v1/agent/service/deregister PUT requests to specified agents (supports service-id lists, parsing curl, agents file, dry-run, optional ACL token). No unrelated binaries or environment variables are requested.
dimensions.label: Purpose & Capability
dimensions.name: purpose_capability

dimensions.detail: Runtime instructions tell the agent to run the included Python script with user-supplied agent addresses, curl text, or an agents file. The script only reads an agents file if explicitly provided and only sends HTTP requests to the host(s) the user supplies. It does not read arbitrary system state or hidden files, nor does it send data to any hard-coded external endpoints.
dimensions.label: Instruction Scope
dimensions.name: instruction_scope

dimensions.detail: No install spec is provided (instruction-only + an included script). There is no download/remote install step; the script runs locally with Python. This is low-risk and proportionate for the described task.
dimensions.label: Install Mechanism
dimensions.name: install_mechanism

dimensions.detail: The skill declares no required environment variables or primary credential. The script accepts an optional --token parameter for Consul ACL tokens, which is appropriate and minimal for performing authenticated deregisters.
dimensions.label: Credentials
dimensions.name: environment_proportionality

dimensions.detail: always:false and default model invocation settings are appropriate. The skill does not persist or modify other skills or global agent configuration and has no elevated platform privileges.
dimensions.label: Persistence & Privilege
dimensions.name: persistence_privilege

llm.guidance: This skill appears to do exactly what it says: it will send HTTP PUT requests to the Consul agent URLs you provide to deregister service instances. Before using it: (1) prefer --dry-run first to verify which requests will be sent; (2) double-check the service-id and agent list (a wrong service-id or wrong host could deregister the wrong instance or target unintended systems); (3) only provide a Consul ACL token if you trust the environment where this runs (the token is included as an X-Consul-Token header when supplied); (4) the script will read any agents file path you pass — do not pass a sensitive system file by mistake; (5) ensure Python3 is available locally. Overall the skill is internally consistent and minimal, but treat deregistration as a destructive action and run with caution in production.
